expected_behavior: All provider writers accept A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, SRV, and CAA records.
MX records require priority and propagate it to provider payloads.
Namecheap setHosts renders HostName, RecordType, Address, TTL, and MXPref fields for supported records.
Route53 renders MX records as priority-prefixed ResourceRecord values.
Cloudflare and Route53 normalize provider FQDN records to zone-relative names before reconciliation.
execution_body.goal: Open provider-backed DNS apply support for A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, SRV, and CAA records while preserving owner-scoped reconciliation and fail-closed provider writes.

issues.description: npmctl schema v2 accepts dns_records and npmctl-namecheap exposes Namecheap record inspection, but plan/apply do not reconcile DNS records or call namecheap.domains.dns.setHosts. Site DNS workflows can validate, doctor, plan, and apply successfully while Namecheap records remain unchanged. Fix requires a DNS reconciliation layer, provider write protocol, Namecheap setHosts support, owner-scoped delete rules, read-only provider fail-closed behavior, and tests for A/CNAME create/update, stale owned record removal, unmanaged record preservation, missing Namecheap client IP handling, and mixed NPM plus DNS plans.
issues.title: Namecheap DNS apply does not mutate provider records
